title: Methyl ester sulfonate suppresses leydig cell steroidogenesis by targeting the GATA2/TGF-beta1/SMAD signaling axis.
authors: Ren, Ke; Hu, Liehai; Zeng, Derui; Chen, Junhan; Yang, Fenglian; Lin, Zongyu; Gan, Weidong; Wang, Junli; Li, Dongmei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究甲基酯磺酸盐通过靶向GATA2/TGF-beta1/SMAD轴抑制睾丸间质细胞类固醇生成，涉及转录因子GATA2与DNA结合及分子对接，但核心是毒理学机制而非TF-DNA互作建模，方法上仅用分子对接和实验验证，AI/物理模拟深度有限。
abstract: Exposure to environmental pollutants during development has been implicated in causing reproductive dysfunction in adult male mice, yet the specific molecular mechanisms by which certain pollutants induce such damage remain poorly understood. Methyl ester sulfonate (MES), a widely used anionic surfactant marketed as a "green" alternative, lacks a comprehensive assessment of its reproductive toxicity. To address this knowledge gap, we established a mouse model of developmental exposure, administering MES (0.06, 0.6, and 6 mg/L) via drinking water from gestational day (GD) 8.5 to postnatal day (PND) 56. Our results showed that developmental MES exposure induced significant histopathological alterations in adult male testes, including impaired blood-testis barrier (BTB) integrity, disorganized spermatocyte alignment, seminiferous tubule vacuolation, and testicular fibrosis. These structural defects were accompanied by significantly reduced serum testosterone and impaired spermatogenesis. Mechanistically, we combined RNA sequencing, molecular docking, and cell thermal shift assay-Western blotting (CETSA-WB) to uncover a novel pathway in Leydig cells (LCs). We demonstrated that MES directly bound to and stabilized the transcription factor GATA binding protein 2 (GATA2), which in turn activated the transforming growth factor-beta1 (TGF-beta1)/SMAD signaling pathway. This cascade suppressed luteinizing hormone receptor (LHR) expression, ultimately impairing testosterone synthesis. This study provides the first mechanistic evidence of MES induced reproductive toxicity in mammals, challenging its safety profile and highlighting a novel GATA2/TGF-beta1/LHR axis that governs steroidogenesis. Our findings underscore the urgent need for a thorough environmental risk assessment of MES.
abstract_zh: 发育期间暴露于环境污染物已被认为与成年雄性小鼠生殖功能障碍相关，然而某些污染物诱导此类损伤的具体分子机制仍知之甚少。甲基酯磺酸盐（MES），一种广泛使用的阴离子表面活性剂，被标榜为“绿色”替代品，但其生殖毒性缺乏全面评估。为填补这一知识空白，我们建立了一个发育暴露小鼠模型，通过饮水从妊娠第8.5天（GD 8.5）至出生后第56天（PND 56）给予MES（0.06、0.6和6 mg/L）。我们的结果表明，发育期MES暴露诱导成年雄性小鼠睾丸出现显著的组织病理学改变，包括血睾屏障（BTB）完整性受损、精母细胞排列紊乱、生精小管空泡化及睾丸纤维化。这些结构缺陷伴随血清睾酮显著降低和精子发生受损。在机制上，我们结合RNA测序、分子对接和细胞热位移分析-蛋白质印迹法（CETSA-WB），在Leydig细胞（LCs）中发现了一条新通路。我们证明MES直接结合并稳定转录因子GATA结合蛋白2（GATA2），进而激活转化生长因子-β1（TGF-beta1）/SMAD信号通路。该级联反应抑制黄体生成素受体（LHR）表达，最终损害睾酮合成。本研究提供了MES诱导哺乳动物生殖毒性的首个机制证据，挑战了其安全性，并揭示了一个调控类固醇生成的新型GATA2/TGF-beta1/LHR轴。我们的发现强调了对MES进行彻底环境风险评估的迫切需求。
